headline: Maui Planning Commission

meeting.summary: The commission approved five homes in Lāhainā and Outrigger resort upgrades with added beach parking and shoreline conditions.
meeting.recap: The Maui Planning Commission met August 25th, 2026.[[0:00:32]] The applicant estimated the homes would use 2,710 gallons of water per day.[[0:14:39]] One testifier asked the commission to deny or defer the permit.[[0:28:12]] The department recommended approval with 10 conditions.[[1:52:28]] Staff said the project adds no hotel rooms.[[2:20:11]] The applicant estimated water use would drop 39,382 gallons per day.[[2:47:12]] The applicant committed to 20 more public beach parking stalls, for 30 total.[[2:58:49]] Commissioners made five stalls open 24 hours for Hawaiian cultural practices.[[5:47:28]] They required a state certified shoreline survey every 10 years, first due by August 31st, 2036.[[5:50:05]] They required a sea level rise mitigation plan.[[6:03:29]] They required the sidewalk in front of the property be removed, relocated or modified by August 31st, 2031.[[6:19:58]] The next meeting is September 8th.[[6:26:52]]
decided: The commission added a condition requiring a sea level rise mitigation plan.
The commission adopted the sidewalk condition.
meeting.next: The September 8th meeting will include a council resolution and zoning changes for the Maui Research and Technology Park.
